text:
Alex M: heads-up — compliance asked whether our audit export can show the exact actor and auth-context when a routing policy was changed, including automated rollbacks. they need to know who/why and which service performed the change :eyes:
Priya S: are they asking for system-actor attribution (e.g. autoscaler/rollout service) + user who triggered? or just the human initiator?
Marco V: both. for incidents audits they want chain-of-action: human -> canary job -> automated rollback. currently our change events only store 'actor_id' and a free-form 'reason'.
Sam R: we also strip downstream system ids for PII reasons. question: do we keep system service names as principals or redact them?
Jin L: compliance preference: human identity must be preserved. system actors can be pseudonymized unless explicitly requested. there should be a redaction flag on export.
Alex M: what would redaction modes look like? propose enum: none | partial | pii_only. partial = keep service names, redact machine ids. pii_only = remove email/ids but keep role.
Priya S: that sounds reasonable. also they want the "auth_context" — e.g. token scope / service account / ip / session id — included for every change so audit can validate permission boundaries.
Marco V: implementation note: adding full auth_context to every event will bloat the stream. export API should support streaming NDJSON and a content_profile param to select detail level. sample API:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports
-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
-d '{"start":"2025-06-01T00:00:00Z","end":"2025-06-01T06:00:00Z","redaction":"partial","include_system":false,"content_profile":"auth_plus_diff"}'```
Sam R: +1 for streaming NDJSON. also need an anchor for diffing — if routing policy changed, include a compact diff: {"before":"..","after":"..","path":"/routes/priority"} so security can link to exact config fragment. small, structured diffs, not full blobs.
Jin L: re: PII: we should redact emails and IPs by default. team can request exports with 'pii_retention=true' but that should be gated behind a compliance approval step.
Priya S: UX question: in Console export modal, show redaction level and a checkbox "Include automated system actors" with tooltip: "Includes rollout/canary service names for chain-of-action investigations". default off for non-enterprise customers.
Marco V: backend: we can add a propagation field 'trigger_chain': ["actor:alex","job:policy-canary-42","svc:rollbacker-1"]. each entry is small token, expansion only if content_profile requests full context.
Alex M: audit-bot queued an export test to validate format. audit-bot: export job 5872 queued (ndjson, partial redaction) — link: https://console.redwood.ai/exports/5872
audit-bot: status update — job 5872 completed, 3.2MB, 420 events. download: https://console.redwood.ai/exports/5872/download
Sam R: can someone try the export and check that the trigger_chain contains pseudonyms for system services and includes session_id when content_profile=auth_plus_diff?
Priya S: i'll run manual check and raise a tiny UX tweak: show an in-console diff preview for first 5 events, not the whole file. helps compliance confirm they picked the right redaction level.
Jin L: also add a minimal retention metadata header to exports: exported_by / export_reason / approval_ticket. makes downstream storage audits simpler.
Marco V: noted. @Alex M i'll add the change schema patch + example NDJSON sample to the PR. cc @Priya S for UX copy.
Alex M: perfect. next steps: Marco to add schema + endpoint, Jin to draft redaction policy doc, Priya to mock modal copy. Sam to smoke-test export job and confirm no PII leaks. I'll follow up with compliance next week. :thumbsup:
